data.prompt: Insert a counter variable in the function to count how many times the line that computes a new candidate value (the expression "table[i-1][c-w] + v") is executed. Run the function on a small instance (e.g., weights=[1,2,3], values=[6,10,12], capacity=5) and report the counter value together with the total number of (i,c) table entries (which is (len(weights)+1)*(capacity+1)).
data.trace_question: How does the number of times you actually compute a new candidate value compare to the total number of distinct (i,c) states in the table? Does any state get recomputed more than once?
data.expected_insight: The counter will be at most the number of distinct states, showing that each sub‑problem is evaluated only once – the memoisation property. Any belief that the recursion’s branching factor still drives the cost is contradicted because the cached results prevent repeated work.
